# Unibox

> One immutable Dart description of a screen, rendered natively by Flutter and as HTML/CSS by Jaspr.

Unibox is a Dart 3.13 workspace of four packages. `packages/unibox_core` holds the
node tree and the design tokens and has no dependencies at all; `packages/unibox_flutter`
and `packages/unibox_jaspr` are two renderers of the same tree; `packages/unibox_conformance`
holds one table of expected presentation that both renderer suites are checked
against, so the two renderings cannot drift apart silently.

Paths in this file are relative to the repository root. This is an index: the rules
a coding agent needs are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), and every other document
assumes you have read the README's node sections.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): the instruction set for a coding agent — non-negotiable
  rules, repository map, commands, and the touch points for a token, a node type,
  a parity fix or an example change.
- [README.md](README.md): the user guide. One section per node, with the parameter
  tables, typography, motion, semantics, and what the host owns.
- [design.md](design.md): why the model looks like this — defaults, precedence,
  dimensions, parity, interaction, non-goals, compatibility.

## Packages

- [unibox_core](packages/unibox_core/README.md): the model — nodes, tokens,
  defaults, validation. Pure Dart; never imports `dart:ui`, Flutter or Jaspr.
- [unibox_flutter](packages/unibox_flutter/README.md): the Flutter renderer
  (`renderFlutter`, `node.toWidget()`), node by node, with what differs from the web.
- [unibox_jaspr](packages/unibox_jaspr/README.md): the Jaspr renderer
  (`renderJaspr`, `node.toComponent()`), the CSS it emits, and the document work it
  leaves to the host.
- [unibox_conformance](packages/unibox_conformance/README.md): the presentation
  contract — `BoxAppearance`, `boxCases`, `TextAppearance`, `textCases` — and the
  line between "the same" and "close enough".

## Working on the repository

- [tool/verify.sh](tool/verify.sh): format check, analysis and the seven test
  suites, the way CI runs them. `--fast` skips the suites, `--docs` adds `dart doc`.
- [.github/workflows/ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml): what continuous integration
  actually runs, including the docs job that fails on a `dart doc` warning.
- [TASK_PLAN.md](TASK_PLAN.md): what is built, the decisions taken, and the
  `Deferred` list that is deliberately out of scope.
- [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md): the human release checklist. CI never publishes.
- [example/README.md](example/README.md): the two pages shared by a Flutter app and
  a static site, and how each host answers what a tree cannot know.

## Optional

- [analysis_options.yaml](analysis_options.yaml): the strict analyzer settings and
  the enabled lints.
- [packages/unibox_core/CHANGELOG.md](packages/unibox_core/CHANGELOG.md),
  [packages/unibox_flutter/CHANGELOG.md](packages/unibox_flutter/CHANGELOG.md),
  [packages/unibox_jaspr/CHANGELOG.md](packages/unibox_jaspr/CHANGELOG.md): the
  unreleased changes, which is where a new token is described for the user.
- [example/unibox_example_shared/lib/](example/unibox_example_shared/lib/): the
  example trees as plain Dart, the arrangement to copy for a real application.
